blocks.prompt: 19. Show that the sum of \(n\) A.Ms. between \(a\) and \(b\) is \(n\) times the single A.M. between them.
blocks.explanation:
A proof. The \(n\) A.M.s together with \(a\) and \(b\) make an A.P. of \(n + 2\) terms.
We must show: (sum of the \(n\) A.M.s) \(= n \times \frac{a + b}{2}\).
Plan: sum the whole A.P., then take away \(a\) and \(b\).
steps:
Given: \(A_1, A_2, \dots, A_n\) are \(n\) A.M.s between \(a\) and \(b\).
To prove: \(A_1 + A_2 + \dots + A_n = n \cdot \dfrac{a + b}{2}\).
Method: By definition \(a, A_1, A_2, \dots, A_n, b\) are in A.P. This A.P. has \(n + 2\) terms, first term \(a\), last term \(b\), so its sum is easy to write.

The single A.M.
\[A = \dfrac{a + b}{2}\]
Why: One A.M. between \(a\) and \(b\) is the middle term of \(a, A, b\), i.e. half their sum.

Sum of the whole A.P.
\[a + A_1 + \dots + A_n + b\]
\[= \dfrac{n + 2}{2}(a + b)\]
Why: \(S = \frac{\text{number of terms}}{2}(\text{first} + \text{last})\) with \(n + 2\) terms.

Remove \(a\) and \(b\)
\[A_1 + \dots + A_n\]
\[= \dfrac{n + 2}{2}(a + b) - (a + b)\]
\[= (a + b)\left(\dfrac{n + 2}{2} - 1\right)\]
\[= \dfrac{n}{2}(a + b)\]
Why: Take out the common factor \((a + b)\); \(\frac{n + 2}{2} - \frac{2}{2} = \frac{n}{2}\).

Compare with the single A.M.
\[\dfrac{n}{2}(a + b) = n \cdot \dfrac{a + b}{2}\]
\[= nA\]
Why: This is \(n\) times the single A.M.

Check with numbers
3 A.M.s between 2 and 14: \(d = \frac{14 - 2}{4} = 3\), so they are \(5, 8, 11\).
\[5 + 8 + 11 = 24\]
\[3 \times \dfrac{2 + 14}{2} = 3 \times 8 = 24 \;\checkmark\]
Why: The result holds in a numerical case.
blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: \(A_1 + A_2 + \dots + A_n = n \cdot \frac{a + b}{2}\), i.e. \(n\) times the single A.M.
